newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - April 4.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - Factors to watch - April 4.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Friday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** India's federal budget for 1997/98 is likely to be approved in parliament only after Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda faces a confidence vote on April 11, newspapers say
** India's ruling coalition and newfound rival, Congress party, pursue war of nerves in political crisis as Hindu nationalists hope for snap polls that could thrust them into power
** Congress party says it will press ahead with its effort to topple Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, but the ruling coalition predicts its rival will opt for a face-saving bargain to avert elections
** United Front leaders say talks are under way to explore a possible settlement to the crisis, which has held hostage the path-breaking, tax-cutting budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year

** United Front says it is prepared to discuss a structured coordination on policy issues, an understanding on specific programmes and perhaps electoral adjustments in the future with the Congress. However, there is no question of either changing their leader, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, or sharing power with the Congress, Times of India newspaper reports
** Truck owners harden stance after government asks army to move goods as two million vehicles keep off roads for fourth day of crippling strike
** The indefinite truck strike has badly affected India's exports and is threatening to paralyse the entire economy, business leaders say
** Oman says an ambitious subsea natural gas pipeline project linking Oman and India does not look possible at present due to technical problems and lack of adequate gas reserves
** Robust sales to power sector drive 1996/97 (April-March) net profit of equipment maker Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd (BHEL) sharply above market expectations
BHEL says its net profit surges nearly 34 percent to 4.68 billion rupees ($130 million), from 3.5 billion in 1995/96
Analysts say results beat market expectations with average consensus net forecast pegged as low as 3.8 billion rupees
** State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) says it produces 28.7 million tonnes of crude oil in 1996/97
The company says the 1996/97 output was "marginally lower" that the targetted output. It did not give output figures of 1995/96
ONGC says its net profit climbs to 19.75 billion rupees in 1996/97, from 19.45 billion in the previous year
** Tata Industries says it has not yet sought replacements to help rescue a $600 million tie-up with Singapore Airlines to launch a domestic venture, now blocked by an aviation policy change
** Political crisis will hit a keenly-awaited $350 million
issue of global equity by largest refiner Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) as crucial oil sector reforms are put on hold, analysts say
MARKETS:
** Bombay stocks expected to open weak on news of new twist in country's six-day old political crisis. End-account factors also seen putting pressure on prices

** Bombay's top 30-share .BSESN index gains 0.60 pct at 3.559.65 on Thursday; National exchange index up 0.71 pct at 1,009.30, Delhi index drops 0.15 pct at 750.02, Calcutta 0.35 pct at 435.90; Madras gains 0.74 pct 3,439.91
